discovery: Quantum control of macroscopic mechanical motion: cavity optomechanics and mechanical oscillators in the quantum ground state

nominees.name: Tobias J. Kippenberg
nominees.affiliation: École Polytechnique Fédérale de Lausanne (EPFL), Switzerland

nominees.name: Markus Aspelmeyer
nominees.affiliation: University of Vienna and IQOQI Vienna, Austria

nominees.name: Andrew N. Cleland
nominees.affiliation: Pritzker School of Molecular Engineering, University of Chicago, USA

motivation: For decades mechanical resonators were classical sensors limited by thermal noise. The nominees showed that engineered mechanical objects containing billions of atoms can be brought into the quantum regime and controlled there. Kippenberg and Aspelmeyer established radiation-pressure cavity optomechanics, demonstrating resolved-sideband cooling, strong coupling, optomechanically induced transparency, and measurement at and beyond the standard quantum limit. Cleland, with Martinis, placed a piezoelectric resonator in its quantum ground state using a superconducting qubit and created single phonons, the first quantum control of a human-made mechanical object. These experiments rest on ingenious measurement schemes treated with rigorous quantitative models of quantum noise and back-action. The resulting toolbox now underpins quantum-limited force and displacement sensing, microwave-to-optical transducers for quantum networks, squeezed and entangled mechanical states, and new tests of quantum mechanics and gravity at macroscopic scales.
